title: Request Fidelity Protector and Sampling Orchestrator
creator: Aisha Raman
description:
Problem statement:

Our current SDK middleware makes sampling decisions early and mutates request metadata in ways that make later stages (edge proxies, backend workers) unable to deterministically correlate or accept/reject traces for cost-sensitive customers. This causes: inconsistent sampling rates across services, difficulty debugging high-latency customer requests, and occasional leakage of sensitive headers into span attributes.

Goal:
Introduce a lightweight Request Fidelity Protector (RFP) layer + Sampling Orchestrator that: 1) captures a canonical request snapshot at ingress, 2) produces deterministic but nonce-like trace prefix IDs for downstream dedup/merge, 3) centralizes sampling budget signalling for per-customer/route policies (without blocking critical low-latency paths), and 4) enforces attribute scrubbing rules before exporting spans. The solution must be small enough to ship in SDKs (JS/Python/Go) and be pluggable as server middleware for our edge and runtime components.

Why this matters:
- Enables consistent end-to-end sampling decisions while preserving per-tenant budgets.
- Improves signal fidelity for latency/error dashboards (we can attribute tail latencies to the right requests).
- Reduces sensitive data sent to tracing backends (compliance).

High-level proposal:
1) Request Fidelity Protector (SDK + middleware component)
   - At ingress (edge or SDK entry), compute a deterministic request fingerprint using method/path/first-8-bytes-of-body-or-hash plus an optional customer secret salt (if tenant-opted).
   - Attach a short trace_prefix header (10-12 hex chars) that is used by downstream services to tag spans for deterministic grouping. This is not the full trace id; the runtime still generates tokenized trace IDs as usual.
   - Capture a minimal canonical snapshot (request_time, route, client_id, anonymized headers list) and include a signed metadata blob for backend-only use. The blob is small (<512 bytes) and HMACed with a service key.

2) Sampling Orchestrator (non-blocking, local-first policy)
   - Local SDK/middleware keeps a tiny token bucket per-tenant (memory-only) with configurable refill rates pulled from server policies.
   - For each incoming request, RFP suggests a sampling decision: sample (record full spans), light-sample (record only error/span-summary), or skip. If local budget is exhausted, fall back to probabilistic sampling based on deterministic prefix to keep reproducibility.
   - Periodic async sync to central policy service for budget adjustments and emergency-wide overrides (rate-limited).

3) Attribute Scrubber and Export Hook
   - Before export, the exporter runs a scrubber using a tenant-aware allowlist/denylist. Patterns are configurable via Console (UI will be added separately).
   - Scrubber can redact or hash attributes. It must be fast and deterministic.

Engineering constraints and non-goals:
- Non-goal: full downstream distributed sampling coordination for all services (we aim for local-first with deterministic fallbacks).
- Must not add blocking network calls on the hot path. All external syncs must be async and rate-limited.
- Keep per-request overhead below 200ns in hot SDK paths (microbenchmark target).

Compatibility and rollout:
- Implement RFP in: SDK JS (node + browser), SDK Python, SDK Go, and server middleware for edge-proxy and runtime container.
- Backwards compatibility: if trace_prefix header exists in older format, translator layer will accept and map into new canonical blob.

Observability and dashboards:
- Emit metrics: sampling_decisions_total{tenant,decision}, sampling_budget_headroom{tenant}, scrubber_redactions_total{tenant,rule}, rfp_fingerprint_collisions_total.
- Dashboards: add a per-tenant sampling headroom view and a request-fidelity heatmap to the latency/error dashboards (PM/Console work will hook into these metrics).

Acceptance criteria (see separate field):

Rollout plan:
1) Library prototypes and microbenchmarks (ENG.INTERNAL-branch) — 2 weeks.
2) Server middleware + end-to-end CI harness (canary on staging) — 1 week.
3) Gradual rollout: 10% of traffic -> 25% -> 100% with monitoring gates for budget and error rates.

Security compliance:
- HMAC keys for metadata blobs stored in KMS.
- Scrubber rules auditable via Console; scrubber must default to deny-sensitive-headers to avoid regressions.

Docs and training:
- Update SDK docs with migration notes and configuration knobs.
- Include sample rules for common PII patterns.
acceptance_criteria: RFP implemented in JS, Python, and Go SDKs and server middleware with feature flag toggles
Deterministic trace_prefix attached at ingress for >99.95% of test requests in staging
Local sampling token buckets respect per-tenant budgets and fall back deterministically when exhausted
Attribute scrubber applied in exporter with configurable rules and no PII leaks in staging run
Metric emitters for sampling decisions and budget headroom are recorded and visible in Grafana/Console
E2E latency regression <2% p95 compared to baseline on representative workloads

2025-02-12 - Diego Morales: Started JS SDK prototype; initial fingerprint function uses murmur3 on first 512 bytes and path. Collision rate looks acceptable in local sim.
2025-02-14 - Lina Park: Server middleware draft complete; needs integration tests with edge-proxy. Will add translation layer for older trace_prefix formats.

2025-02-16 - Ravi Patel: Scrubber POC ready. Default rule set redacts Authorization, Cookie, and any header matching /.*(ssn|dob|card).*/i. Performance microbenchmarks show ~80ns per attribute check when precompiled patterns used.
2025-02-18 - Security review (Nina Cho): Requested explicit KMS key rotation plan and audits for the metadata blobs. Marking security_review_required true.
